note: Routes that cannot be driven by any gauntlet tier today. Every entry names WHY and WHO. A route with no entry and no observation appears in the report's 'NO stated reason at all' row, which is the row that should make someone uncomfortable. 'No tier drives it yet' is a real and admissible reason; it is deliberately NOT phrased as 'blocked' when nothing structural prevents it, so that a missing test never launders itself into an external blocker. Rules: most specific matching rule wins; a trailing '*' is a prefix glob; keep an entry only while it is true, and delete it the moment its route executes.

Dealer accelerator, not part of the seven-role successor release set; no tier deploys it. THE FRAME-CLEANLINESS HALF OF THIS ROW IS RESOLVED (W2h, 2026-08-27): measured at c3c4950 and again at 5e25f8e, cargo build-sbf on programs/dclutch-dealer-accelerator-sbf emits ZERO 'overwrites values in the frame' diagnostics, against 253 measured on the same tree at the immediately preceding HEAD. TA-DLR's root cause was correct and is independent of the fix: with `no-entrypoint` set, dclutch-trading-sbf compiles without its own #[global_allocator], which leaves __rust_alloc an opaque extern that cannot be folded at its call sites and spills hot_v3::process_hot_execution_v3 past the SBPF v0 4,096-byte frame. What changed is the headroom, not the allocator: process_hot_execution_v3 used 3,904 bytes of that frame with the outgoing-argument area filling the rest, and c3c4950 split it into an authentication half (3,008 bytes) and an execution half (2,496), which absorbs the opaque extern. TA-DLR's two-edit patch is therefore NOT required for this row and is NOT applied. It remains the principled fix for the underlying incoherence -- a no-entrypoint library build of Trading still runs Hot code under whichever allocator its host executable installs, not the one the shipped Trading program uses -- and if it is taken: re-measure on top of c3c4950 rather than against the stale 253; land both halves together (either alone is a duplicate or a missing #[global_allocator], both hard errors); and per W1f keep admit_heap_frame_v1 and lift_declared_heap_profile_v1 reachable in the SHIPPED ELF, where DCLTPCB1 depends on them on chain now. Widening the cfg does not move the shipped build either way, since `no-entrypoint` is off there and both predicates already evaluate the same. The emitted accelerator .so was never contaminated in any case: process_hot_execution_v3 is dead-stripped from it.
blocked.owner: TA-DLR (the campaign); frame blocker cleared by W2h, the allocator-coherence question is an owner decision

blocked.reason: STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE, not merely un-driven. Every route of programs/dclutch-series-sbf ends in a Core CPI that Core refuses by construction: the adapter sends exactly SERIES_CORE_REQUEST_BYTES_V1 (336) bytes with no receipt tail (series-sbf/src/lib.rs:844), while Core's dispatch for that magic requires a tail of CLAIMS_FOUNDING_RECEIPT_BYTES_V5 (1008) or PROJECTED_CUSTODY_LOCK_RECEIPT_BYTES_V1 (320), both filtered on start >= 336, so a bare request falls through to CoreSbfError::Instruction. Core also has NO handler for SeriesCoreActionV1::{Prepare, Expire, Close}; series_open.rs:253 and series_consume.rs:296 both require Consume. So no tier anyone writes can execute these four routes or raise these twelve codes. It is also the only consumer of the v1 dclutch-series-codec; Core, Trading, series-shadow and the operator are all on dclutch-series-v3-kernel, whose Core seam DOES execute (see core/series_consume::process). Full argument: docs/evidence/SERIES_ADAPTER_CORE_SEAM_2026_08_27.md. This needs an owner DECISION -- delete the superseded path per AGENTS.md, or write an ADR for the Core-side Prepare/Expire/Close seam -- not a test.
blocked.owner: UNASSIGNED — needs an owner decision, not a test (TA-SER, 2026-08-27)

The test caller exists (programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/test-programs/terminal-settlement-caller) and the route needs no open Market and no Hot execution, so a ProgramTest can reach it -- the work is the prestate, not the wiring. Its 35-account frame is the SignedDeltaV3 fixed 20 plus one runtime Position plus fourteen terminal accounts, and authenticate_and_prepare requires, beyond what the shared Product/LBV2 fixture already builds: (a) a Core Market in a TERMINAL state -- `terminal_receipt` Some and `terminal_winner` below the Product outcome count -- where compile_product_lbv2_fixture_v2 builds Phase::Open with terminal_receipt None; (b) a finalized composition-exposure record and vacant staging cursor under COMPOSITION_EXPOSURE_SCHEMA_ID_V3 (dclutch-representation-composition-v3-kernel); (c) a finalized terminal-coordinate record and staging cursor under TERMINAL_COORDINATE_SCHEMA_RELEASE_ID_V2 whose scenario matches the basis kind (CategoricalQ1 in the shared fixture); (d) the whole Custody leg -- a CustodyReplayV1, a Hoard token account, a recipient token account, the custody-authority PDA and a real token program, i.e. the fixture programs/dclutch-custody-sbf/tests/program_test.rs already builds; and (e) a Realm record plus staging cursor. Nothing here is structurally blocked; it is the union of two existing fixtures plus two record kinds nobody has compiled in a test yet.
